t: This is Queen Street, running from Upper Thames Street in the south up to Cheapside in the north. It and King Street were laid out new after the Great Fire of 1666, cutting across older routes in the City. They were the only notable new streets to come out of the fire's destruction. The name honours Catherine of Braganza, who was queen of England, Scotland and Ireland from 1662 to 1685 through her marriage to Charles the Second. After his death she returned to Portugal and served as regent for her brother.
